sections.title: A mysterious organ
sections.prompt: Which famous artist was so confused by the heart that he gave up studying it?
sections.hint: He was an Italian Renaissance artist named in the first few seconds.
sections.feedback_correct: Right! The heart confused Leonardo da Vinci so much that he gave up studying it.
sections.feedback_wrong: Listen for the artist's name right at the start of the video.

sections.title: Why the valves stay hidden
sections.prompt: Why is it so hard to see a heart working? Pick the three reasons given.

cards.text: An exposed heart means the body perishes quickly
You can't see through the blood vessels
The heart beats too fast to film
Doctors are not allowed to study it
The valves are too small to see

sections.hint: Think about what happens if the heart is taken out, and what blood is like.
sections.feedback_correct: Exactly. The body perishes quickly, the vessels can't be seen through and opaque blood hides the valves.
sections.feedback_wrong: Listen again for the three reasons the valves are hard to see working.

sections.title: How the heart gets taught
sections.prompt: Complete what the video says about how heart function is usually taught.
sections.text: Internet searches point to crude [[models]], diagrams or animations. The next best thing is simply to [[cut]] it open and [[label]] the parts.
sections.hint: Teachers accept heart function 'cannot be demonstrated', so they dissect and name the parts instead.
sections.feedback_correct: Yes. Because heart function seems impossible to demonstrate, lessons cut the heart open and label its parts.
sections.feedback_wrong: Listen for what internet searches point to, and the 'next best thing' teachers do.

sections.title: The figure-eight circulation
sections.prompt: Put the path of blood in a figure-eight circulation in order.
items: Blood leaves the first heart pump
It returns to the second heart pump
The second pump sends it to the body
It comes back to the first pump
sections.hint: The lungs come before the body.
sections.feedback_correct: Spot on: pump one, lungs, pump two, body, then back to pump one. That's why it's a figure-eight, not a dual circulation.
sections.feedback_wrong: Listen to how blood travels between the two heart pumps, the lungs and the body.

sections.title: A medic for a day
sections.prompt: Fact or fiction? Decide for each statement.

statements.text: You need a whole fresh heart, like one from a sheep or pig.
An intact heart in water pumps when you squeeze it by hand.
Water doesn't enter the heart cleanly enough for the pump to work.
Leonardo da Vinci solved the problem with this experiment.

sections.hint: The first try with a whole heart in water doesn't work, and the video says why.
sections.feedback_correct: Correct. A whole heart in water won't pump when squeezed because water doesn't enter it cleanly enough.
sections.feedback_wrong: Listen to what happens when the whole heart is squeezed under water, and why.

sections.title: Trimming the atria
sections.prompt: Sort the parts: what gets cut off, and what is left?
sections.hint: The veins are attached to the atria.
sections.feedback_correct: Great sorting. Cutting off the atria removes their incoming veins, leaving the ventricles and the two major arteries.
sections.feedback_wrong: Listen to which chambers are cut off and which two vessels rise like white columns.

sections.title: The valves in action
sections.prompt: Match each term to what the video says about it.

pairs.right: The ventricular valve in the right ventricle
The ventricular valve in the left ventricle
Where water squirts out when the right ventricle is squeezed
The number of beats a heart gives in its lifetime

sections.hint: The tricuspid is on the right.
sections.feedback_correct: Well matched. The valves open and close like parachutes and barely wear out over 2 billion beats.
sections.feedback_wrong: Listen for the names of the two ventricular valves and the lifetime number of beats.

sections.title: Feel your own pump
sections.prompt: One word in this quote is wrong. Tap it.
sections.text: Understanding how this dependable inner pump works gives new resonance to the feeling you get when you run a race, drink too much {{water|caffeine}} or catch the eye of the one you love.
sections.hint: Which drink makes your heart race?
sections.feedback_correct: You spotted it: the video says 'drink too much caffeine'.
sections.feedback_wrong: Listen closely to the three moments that make your heart race.
